form.zh: 新乐府（七言为主的古诗）
form.en: New Music Bureau ballad (an old-style poem, mostly seven characters a line)

text_note.zh: 这里用课本的写法。原始资料题作“新乐府 卖炭翁”，小序是“苦官市也”；课本题作《卖炭翁》，小序是“苦宫市也”。原始资料的“城上一尺雪”“官使驱将”，课本作“城外一尺雪”“宫使驱将”。“宫市”指皇宫派人到市场买东西，“官”应是“宫”的误写。
text_note.en: This follows the textbook. The source title adds "New Music Bureau" before the poem's name, and its short preface uses a character for "official" where the textbook has "palace": the poem is about the palace market. The source also has "a foot of snow on the city wall" where the textbook has "outside the city", and "official envoy" where the textbook has "palace envoy".

readings.zh: 衣裳在古诗里读 yī cháng，裳指下身穿的裙子一类。现在口语里“衣裳”读 yī shang。
readings.en: In old poems this word for clothes is read yī cháng; cháng was the lower garment. In everyday speech today it is yī shang.
Read niǎn here, meaning to roll over and crush.

readings.zh: 现在课本读 qí。“骑”作名词指骑马的人时，旧读 jì。
readings.en: Textbooks today read it qí. When it means a rider, the old reading is jì.

readings.zh: 将，放在动词后，没有实际意义，读 jiāng。
readings.en: Read jiāng; after a verb it adds no real meaning.
Read jì here, meaning to tie on.

glosses.zh: 伐薪：砍柴。
glosses.en: fá xīn: to cut firewood.

glosses.zh: 南山：长安城南的终南山。
glosses.en: nán shān: the Zhongnan Mountains, south of Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 烟火色：被烟火熏出来的颜色，脸又黑又黄。
glosses.en: yān huǒ sè: the color of smoke and fire; his face is darkened by soot.

glosses.zh: 苍苍：头发灰白的样子。
glosses.en: cāng cāng: gray, turning white.

glosses.zh: 何所营：用来做什么。营，谋求、经营。
glosses.en: hé suǒ yíng: what is it for? Yíng means to seek or provide for.

glosses.zh: 可怜：让人同情。
glosses.en: kě lián: pitiful.

glosses.zh: 晓驾：天刚亮就赶着车。
glosses.en: xiǎo jià: driving the cart at dawn.

glosses.zh: 辗冰辙：车轮压着结冰的车道走。辙，车轮压出的痕迹。
glosses.en: niǎn bīng zhé: rolling along frozen ruts. Zhé is a wheel track.

glosses.zh: 困：累，疲乏。
glosses.en: kùn: worn out.

glosses.zh: 市南门外：长安集市南门的外面。
glosses.en: shì nán mén wài: outside the south gate of the market.

glosses.zh: 翩翩：轻快的样子，这里形容骑马的人得意洋洋。
glosses.en: piān piān: light and quick; here, the riders swagger.

glosses.zh: 黄衣使者：穿黄衣服的宫里太监，是宫市的头头。
glosses.en: huáng yī shǐ zhě: an envoy in yellow, a palace eunuch in charge of the palace market.

glosses.zh: 白衫儿：穿白衣服的手下。
glosses.en: bái shān ér: a lad in white, his helper.

glosses.zh: 文书：公文。
glosses.en: wén shū: an official paper.

glosses.zh: 称敕：说是皇帝的命令。敕，皇帝的命令。
glosses.en: chēng chì: claiming it is the emperor's order. Chì is an order from the emperor.

glosses.zh: 叱：大声吆喝。
glosses.en: chì: to shout at.

glosses.zh: 牵向北：往北拉去。皇宫在长安城北边。
glosses.en: qiān xiàng běi: drag it north. The palace was in the north of Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 宫使：宫里派出来的使者，就是前面的太监。
glosses.en: gōng shǐ: the palace envoys, the eunuchs above.

glosses.zh: 驱将：赶着走。
glosses.en: qū jiāng: to drive away.

glosses.zh: 惜不得：舍不得也没有用。
glosses.en: xī bù dé: he cannot hold on to it, however much it hurts.

glosses.zh: 半匹红纱一丈绫：半匹红纱和一丈绫。纱和绫都是丝织品，当时可以当钱用，但这么一点远远不值一车炭。
glosses.en: bàn pǐ hóng shā yī zhàng líng: half a bolt of red gauze and ten feet of silk. Silk could be used as money then, but this was far less than a cartload of charcoal is worth.

glosses.zh: 充炭直：当作炭的价钱。直，同“值”，价钱。
glosses.en: chōng tàn zhí: as the price of the charcoal. Zhí here means value, price.

translation.zh: 有一个卖炭的老人，
translation.en: There is an old man who sells charcoal.

translation.zh: 在南山里砍柴烧炭。
translation.en: He cuts wood and burns it into charcoal in the Southern Mountains.

translation.zh: 满脸都是灰尘，被烟火熏得又黑又黄，
translation.en: His face is covered with dust, darkened by smoke and fire.

translation.zh: 两边鬓发灰白，十个手指乌黑。
translation.en: The hair at his temples is gray, and his ten fingers are black.

translation.zh: 卖炭得了钱拿来做什么？
translation.en: What does he do with the money from the charcoal?

translation.zh: 换身上穿的衣服、嘴里吃的饭。
translation.en: He buys clothes for his back and food for his mouth.

translation.zh: 可怜他身上的衣服正单薄，
translation.en: Poor man, his clothes are thin,

translation.zh: 心里却担心炭卖不上价，盼着天更冷些。
translation.en: yet he worries the charcoal will sell cheap, and wishes for colder weather.

translation.zh: 夜里城外下了一尺厚的雪，
translation.en: At night a foot of snow falls outside the city.

translation.zh: 天刚亮，他就赶着炭车，轧着冻冰的车道进城。
translation.en: At dawn he drives his cart over the frozen ruts.

translation.zh: 牛累了，人饿了，太阳已经升得很高，
translation.en: The ox is tired, the man is hungry, and the sun is already high.

translation.zh: 他在集市南门外的泥地里歇一歇。
translation.en: He rests in the mud outside the south gate of the market.

translation.zh: 两个骑马的人得意洋洋地过来，是谁呀？
translation.en: Two riders come swaggering up. Who are they?

translation.zh: 是穿黄衣的宫中使者和穿白衫的手下。
translation.en: An envoy in yellow and a lad in white.

translation.zh: 他们手里拿着文书，嘴里说是皇帝的命令，
translation.en: Paper in hand, they say it is the emperor's order.

translation.zh: 掉转车头，吆喝着牛，往北拉去。
translation.en: They turn the cart around, shout at the ox and drag it north.

translation.zh: 一车炭，
translation.en: A cartload of charcoal,

translation.zh: 一千多斤，
translation.en: more than a thousand pounds:

translation.zh: 被宫使赶走了，老人舍不得也没有办法。
translation.en: the palace envoys take it away, and the old man can do nothing.

translation.zh: 他们把半匹红纱和一丈绫，
translation.en: Half a bolt of red gauze and ten feet of silk

translation.zh: 挂在牛头上，就算是炭钱了。
translation.en: they hang on the ox's head, as the price of the charcoal.

background.zh: 这首诗是白居易《新乐府》五十首中的一首，小序说“苦宫市也”，意思是为宫市带给百姓的痛苦而写。宫市是唐朝后期的一种做法：皇宫派太监到市场上“买”东西，常常只给很少的钱，甚至直接抢走，百姓苦不堪言。《新乐府》大约写于唐宪宗元和四年（809年）前后，当时白居易在朝廷做左拾遗，是专门给皇帝提意见的官。
background.en: This is one of Bai Juyi's fifty New Music Bureau ballads. Its short preface says it was written about the suffering caused by the palace market. In the late Tang, the palace sent eunuchs to the markets to "buy" goods. They often paid very little, or just took things, and common people suffered badly. The ballads were written around 809, when Bai Juyi was an Advisor of the Left at court, an official whose job was to point out the emperor's mistakes.

author_note.zh: 白居易（772—846），字乐天，唐代大诗人。他认为写诗要为现实、为百姓说话，《新乐府》就是他这种主张的代表作。他的诗明白好懂，讲故事的本领也很强，《卖炭翁》《琵琶行》《长恨歌》都是用诗讲的故事。
author_note.en: Bai Juyi (772–846), also called Letian, was a great Tang poet. He thought poems should speak about real life and for common people, and the New Music Bureau ballads are his best-known poems of this kind. His poems are clear and easy to follow, and he was a fine storyteller: "The Old Charcoal Seller", "Song of the Pipa" and "Song of Everlasting Regret" all tell stories in verse.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像讲一个小故事。先画出卖炭翁的样子：满脸烟灰，鬓发灰白，十指乌黑，一看就知道他多辛苦。“心忧炭贱愿天寒”最让人心酸：他自己穿得那么单薄，却盼着天更冷，因为天冷炭才能卖个好价钱。下了一场大雪，他高高兴兴地赶车进城，没想到碰上了宫使。两个人一来，拿出文书，把一车炭拉走，只在牛头上挂了一点纱和绫。诗到这里就停了，没有说一句评论的话，但读者心里都明白，也都很气愤。不直说，让事实自己说话，这正是这首诗的力量。
appreciation.en: This poem tells a small story. First it paints the old man: a face full of soot, gray hair at his temples, ten black fingers. One look shows how hard his life is. The saddest line is "his clothes are thin, yet he wishes for colder weather", because only cold weather brings a good price for charcoal. Heavy snow falls, and he drives happily into the city. Then he meets the palace envoys. They show a paper, take the whole cart away, and hang a little gauze and silk on the ox's head. The poem stops there. It says nothing about right or wrong, but every reader understands and feels angry. Letting the facts speak for themselves is the power of this poem.
